In [[mathematics]], the '''Tsen rank''' of a [[field (mathematics)|field]] describes conditions under which a system of [[polynomial equations]] must have a solution in the [[Field (mathematics)|field]].  The concept is named for [[C. C. Tsen]], who introduced their study in 1936.

We consider a system of ''m'' polynomial equations in ''n'' variables over a field ''F''.  Assume that the equations all have constant term zero, so that (0,&nbsp;0,&nbsp;...&nbsp;,0) is a common solution.  We say that ''F'' is a '''T'''<sub>'''''i'''''</sub>-'''field''' if every such system, of degrees ''d''<sub>1</sub>,&nbsp;...,&nbsp;''d''<sub>''m''</sub> has a common non-zero solution whenever 

:<math>n > d_1^i + \cdots + d_m^i. \, </math>

The ''Tsen rank'' of ''F'' is the smallest ''i'' such that ''F'' is a T<sub>''i''</sub>-field.  We say that the Tsen rank of ''F'' is infinite if it is not a T<sub>''i''</sub>-field for any ''i'' (for example, if it is [[formally real field|formally real]]).

==Properties==
* A field has Tsen rank zero [[if and only if]] it is [[Algebraically closed field|algebraically closed]].
* A finite field has Tsen rank 1: this is the [[Chevalley–Warning theorem]].
* If ''F'' is algebraically closed then rational function field ''F''(''X'') has Tsen rank 1.
* If ''F'' has Tsen rank ''i'', then the rational function field ''F''(''X'') has Tsen rank at most ''i''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1.
* If ''F'' has Tsen rank ''i'', then an [[algebraic extension]] of ''F''  has Tsen rank at most&nbsp;''i''.
* If ''F'' has Tsen rank ''i'', then an extension of ''F'' of [[transcendence degree]] ''k'' has Tsen rank at most ''i''&nbsp;+&nbsp;''k''. 
* There exist fields of Tsen rank ''i'' for every integer ''i''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0.

==Norm form==
We define a ''norm form of level i'' on a field ''F'' to be a [[homogeneous polynomial]] of degree ''d'' in ''n''=''d''<sup>''i''</sup> variables with only the trivial zero over ''F'' (we exclude the case ''n''=''d''=1).  The existence of a norm form on level ''i'' on ''F'' implies that ''F'' is of Tsen rank at least ''i''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;1.  If ''E'' is an extension of ''F'' of finite degree ''n''&nbsp;>&nbsp;1, then the field [[norm form]] for ''E''/''F'' is a norm form of level 1.  If ''F'' admits a norm form of level ''i'' then the rational function field ''F''(''X'') admits a norm form of level ''i''&nbsp;+&nbsp;1.  This allows us to demonstrate the existence of fields of any given Tsen rank.

==Diophantine dimension==
The '''Diophantine dimension''' of a field is the smallest natural number ''k'', if it exists, such that the field of is class C<sub>''k''</sub>: that is, such that any homogeneous polynomial of degree ''d'' in ''N'' variables has a non-trivial zero whenever ''N''&nbsp;>&nbsp; ''d''<sup>''k''</sup>.  Algebraically closed fields are of Diophantine dimension 0; [[quasi-algebraically closed field]]s of dimension 1.<ref name=NSW361>{{cite book | title=Cohomology of Number Fields | volume=323 | series=Grundlehren der Mathematischen Wissenschaften | first1=Jürgen | last1=Neukirch | first2=Alexander | last2=Schmidt | first3=Kay | last3=Wingberg | edition=2nd | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | year=2008 | isbn=978-3-540-37888-4 | page=361}}</ref>

Clearly if a field is T<sub>''i''</sub> then it is C<sub>''i''</sub>, and T<sub>0</sub> and C<sub>0</sub> are equivalent, each being equivalent to being algebraically closed.  It is not known whether Tsen rank and Diophantine dimension are equal in general.
